answer: Last week I ranked poster pairs for a print shop. Five pairs a day, and my picks stayed mine. Violet over shale Monday, ferrous gray over bright red Thursday. One taste copied across a thousand identities leaves a thousand identical lists, and the network checks the correlation each round. Each round catches a copy a third of the time, so five rounds catch it nine times in ten. A thousand fakes need a thousand distinct tastes, each a mind or a model. Two real people sometimes love the same poster, so only near-identical lists across all five rounds raise a flag.
